issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the stock in the SealSaloon constructor (instance-level initialization), but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). This is a contradiction: a static field cannot be properly initialized per-instance in the constructor. Students will be confused where and how to initialize the shared static final stock (in the constructor vs. at declaration/static initializer).
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify the intent in the problem statement. Either (A) require stock to be an instance (non-static) final field and instruct students to initialize it in the constructor, or (B) keep the stock static final (shared) and instruct students to initialize it at the declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor). Update the wording so it no longer suggests initializing a static shared field in the instance constructor.

issues.description: The UML and problem description show acceptSupplyDelivery as a public method (+acceptSupplyDelivery), but the reference solution declares acceptSupplyDelivery with package-private visibility (no explicit public). This is a visibility mismatch between the specification/diagram and the solution. Students may expect to implement it as public per the UML and could be confused by the differing visibility in the reference.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the visibility consistent. Either update the UML/problem text to allow package-private visibility for acceptSupplyDelivery, or (preferably) change the reference implementation to declare the method public (public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(...)) so it matches the diagram and the usual expectation from the specification.
